source.title: Interpreting CFD Surrogates through Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a sparse autoencoder as a post-hoc interpretation tool for a CFD surrogate, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, or whether SAE features are complete or canonical units.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE-based temporal, spatial, and vortex-alignment analyses in a CFD surrogate. These are relevant to interpreting SAE features but do not measure the behaviors specified by V1–V6. The reported vortex-alignment scores and localization findings are recorded under fits_no_version. SAE settings, dataset sizes, and referenced results from other papers are not result rows.
record.test_reason: The study applies an SAE as a post-hoc interpretation tool to a MeshGraphNets CFD surrogate. It reports its method's alignment with vorticity regions and its spatial localization. It does not test superposition, capacity, polysemanticity origins, or SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicality. It does not test whether the surrogate's features are sparse or superposed either: it reports no reconstruction or sparsity statistics and no comparison of SAE features to neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one correction. The authors claim SAE saliency outperforms all baselines, yet SAE (entropy) exactly equals embedding-norm on all four metrics in Table 2. The authors' 'consistently outperforms' statement is therefore overstated for the entropy variant.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains an SAE on frozen node embeddings from a MeshGraphNets CFD surrogate and evaluates physical interpretability; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported temporal Jaccard patterns and vortex-alignment scores vary with the SAE coordinate-ranking metric; entropy performs below variance and mean-absolute scoring.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE-coordinate node saliency in a MeshGraphNets CFD surrogate aligns with top-10% vorticity nodes (F1 0.60 variance/mean-abs, 0.55 entropy). This exceeds PCA (0.49) and random (0.09), and entropy ties embedding-norm (0.55).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries on GNN surrogate embeddings yield physically aligned node saliency, depending on the ranking criterion.

fits_no_version.finding: Overlap between global and time-local Top-50 SAE coordinates oscillates with the vortex-shedding period. Entropy ranking gives lower overlap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persistence of salient SAE coordinates over time depends on the saliency ranking metric.

fits_no_version.finding: Aggregated and individual SAE coordinates localize to distinct flow regions (cylinder surface, boundaries, wake). This is shown qualitatively only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual SAE features in a CFD surrogate have spatially distinct footprints.

record.problems: The evidence is from one CFD dataset and one stated surrogate configuration. The temporal comparison is illustrated for a selected testing case, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates. The results assess physical localization and vorticity alignment, not SAE feature completeness or canonicality.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 comparator results for embedding-norm, PCA, and random sampling are omitted because they compare other methods and do not measure the claim versions. Figure-only Jaccard values are recorded as figure-only rather than estimated numerically.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, or feature geometry.
No capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
No analysis of the origins of polysemanticity.
No LLMs. Even for the CFD surrogate, there is no measure of how features spread across neurons, nor any SAE reconstruction or sparsity quality.
No test of completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicality of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a single-dataset (CylinderFlow) workshop-style preprint with no uncertainty estimates. The temporal analysis covers one selected test case. Its 'monosemantic' claims are asserted from qualitative mesh visualizations, not measured. It is not relevant as evidence for V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity competition explains polysemanticity or allocates dedicated dimensions to important features.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study concerns a CFD surrogate, not LLMs, and does not test the stated LLM representation claim.
It evaluates physical interpretability of SAE-derived activity, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

relation.reason: Uses sparse dictionary learning as an interpretation tool without testing superposition or dictionary completeness, stability, or canonicality.

tranche.reason: Applies SAE dictionaries to CFD surrogate interpretation and reports its method's saliency performance; no result tests a listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Rows describe method-performance context; temporal Jaccard measures selection overlap within one dictionary, not feature stability across training runs. Table 2 contradicts the authors' claimed universal superiority: entropy SAE ties embedding-norm on all four metrics.
